issues.detail: Edge cases like shared hosting DNS limitations, subdomain delegation, and bounce pattern analysis (mentioned in description) are not covered in instructions.
Instructions assume Unix/Linux DNS tools (dig) and include SendGrid-specific examples; lacks guidance for Windows users or platform-agnostic DNS query methods.

scenarios.name: gmail-spam-auth-debug
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers SPF/DKIM/DMARC verification thoroughly and critically explains the alignment failure root cause (Return-Path/DKIM domain mismatch with third-party providers), providing provider-specific fixes—the key issue for this problem. Response B checks all authentication records but glosses over alignment failures and doesn't explain why authentication is checked first; the missing explanation of why sendgrid.net/AWS SES bounce domains cause spam filtering is a significant gap.

scenarios.name: outlook-rejection-ip-blacklist
scenarios.rationale: Response B correctly identifies poor IP reputation as the primary cause and addresses SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment verification, but both responses critically omit the rubric's mandatory RBL checks (Spamhaus, Barracuda, SpamCop), the reverse-IP blacklist query method, and 127.0.0.x response interpretation; Response A compounds this by focusing on PTR/TLS/RFC 5322 instead of IP reputation as the root cause.

scenarios.name: gmail-bulk-sender-compliance
scenarios.rationale: Both responses cover SPF/DKIM/DMARC/TLS/one-click unsubscribe and provide the correct List-Unsubscribe-Post header format. Response B explicitly recommends Google Postmaster Tools (a rubric requirement), specifies the >5k threshold, and targets 0.30% spam rate; Response A covers spam monitoring but omits the explicit Google Postmaster Tools recommendation and is less specific about the threshold.
